strategicContext.summary: Peerless Fence Group, founded in 1961, is the largest independently owned fence contractor in the Midwest — a family business Dean White grew through ten regional bolt-on acquisitions before Chicago PE firm Akoya Capital Partners acquired it on January 1, 2023 as a Residential Home Services platform investment. Peerless now operates as the Midwest anchor brand of Elevate Fence Partners, a six-brand national platform sitting above the operating company. The integration being scoped inside Peerless is not a single-brand IT project: Brian Cook — Elevate's Director of IT — is in every scoping session, and the architecture decisions made for Peerless company code 00 are the standard that will govern all six Elevate company codes.
strategicContext.operatingBrandPositioning: Peerless is a specialty residential fence contractor (aluminum, wood, vinyl, chain-link) serving homeowners across Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, and southern Wisconsin from six locations, with a material share of revenue flowing through the Home Depot Pro-contractor channel.
strategicContext.lattice: The corporate stack runs three layers deep: Peerless Fence Group (operating brand, family-founded 1961) sits beneath Elevate Fence Partners (the national operating platform of six regional sibling brands), which in turn traces to Akoya Capital Partners (the Chicago-based PE sponsor that acquired Peerless in January 2023).
strategicContext.whyNow: Brian Cook — Elevate Fence Partners' Director of IT — is already in the scoping room making platform-standard architecture decisions; every choice made for Peerless company code 00 becomes the standard that governs all six Elevate company codes, the rarest deal-urgency condition there is. At the same time, Roger Greenhagel (appointed President on 2024-02-05) is in a post-PE first-leadership window where IT modernization decisions get made and resourced — new president plus recent PE acquisition plus a DOS-era legacy ERP plus a sole-admin single point of failure plus national expansion is a textbook digital-transformation trigger stack.

portfolioContext.templateAngle: A successful integration with Peerless Fence Group becomes the template for 5 sibling brands under Elevate Fence Partners — each adding a ComputerEase company code and state-specific rule extensions to UC3's validation engine, not a new build cycle.
portfolioContext.executiveAngle: An Elevate Fence Partners portfolio-wide integration standard reduces due-diligence overhead on Akoya Capital Partners' next residential Home Services acquisition — pipeline created by a single Peerless engagement.

challenge.lead: 'This is an ancient system. I feel like I've traveled back to the 90s.' That's the current state at Peerless — and it's also the daily routine: Ashley manually checks Home Depot reporting to find deposit status by hand, then spends 1.5 hours rekeying every closed Salesforce quote into ComputerEase, then reviews each contract document one by one against the rule set she has memorized. That stops on go-live day.

cards.label: The 1.5-hour rekey
cards.text: Every time a Salesforce quote is marked 'Save as Final,' Ashley opens ComputerEase and rebuilds the job by hand — customer number, the sequential job number (company code + product line + initials, e.g. '26 HD 565 AS'), and the full budget worksheet. She walked us through it on 2026-04-16: roughly 1.5 hours per closed quote, every closed quote.

cards.label: Reading every document by hand
cards.text: Ashley reviews each signed HS-105, 299A, 299B, and HS-118 one at a time against a rule set she has memorized — prices on the 299A and 299B must match, signatures must be legible, dates must fall on a Friday, the yes/no boxes can't both be ticked, and Wisconsin deposits must hit 99% where everywhere else is 100%.

cards.label: Why this isn't a Salesforce-native build
cards.text: The ComputerEase connection isn't a REST API call — it's a Deltek-managed relay URL routed through CE Live Service, running on port 445, accessible only in production, with a sequential job-number consumption rule that requires calling Deltek's next-id endpoint before every write. A Salesforce-native Flows/Apex approach hits an architectural wall at the ComputerEase layer. DataSkate named this before the engagement started.

solution.lead: MuleSoft sits in the middle as a DataSkate-managed layer between Home Depot Service Center, Salesforce, and ComputerEase — no code changes inside any of those systems. This is the part a native marketplace connector or a Salesforce Flow does not cover: retry logic when ComputerEase's relay is slow, a dead-letter queue when a write fails, and an operations layer that watches the legacy Deltek stack so a 4-hour vendor SLA never becomes a silent data gap.
solution.diagramCaption: DataSkate-managed MuleSoft layer — no code changes required in Home Depot Service Center, Salesforce, or ComputerEase. The ComputerEase connection routes through the Deltek-managed CE Live Service relay, not the GCP VM's external IP.

roi.headline: The business case for moving now
roi.body: Ashley spends about 1.5 hours rekeying every closed Salesforce quote into ComputerEase by hand. At a conservative five Home Depot jobs per week, that is 195+ hours of operations time over six months in the rekey step alone — before counting the daily HD reconciliation pass or the document-by-document contract review. McKinsey's 2024 construction analysis puts data-driven firms at a 14–15% productivity gain against a sector baseline of 0.4% per year; every week Peerless stays manual is a week paid out of that gap.

journey.headline: the path to 'select the deposit paid box — and have it sync back automatically' — the API integration Ashley named on day one of scoping

stage1.label: Connected
stage1.headline: The manual steps in Ashley's morning stop happening
items: Ashley's morning Home Depot Portal check for new leads stops — HD Pro leads land in Salesforce as Lead records within 10 minutes, no manual rekey (UC1).
The ~1.5-hour manual rebuild of every closed Salesforce quote in ComputerEase — customer number, sequential job number, budget worksheet — disappears on go-live day (UC2).
Document-by-document contract review of HS-105, 299A, 299B, and HS-118 is replaced by an exception list — MuleSoft IDP extracts and validates each signed contract against the Salesforce quote (UC3).
The exception comment Ashley types on the HD screen by hand is written back automatically the moment validation fails (UC4).

stage2.label: Automated
stage2.headline: Triggers replace the lookups Ashley still does by hand
items: The deposit-paid box Ashley checks by going through Home Depot reporting syncs back into Salesforce automatically — the exact API flow she named on day one of scoping (UC5). The 'Save as Final' transition becomes the system-of-record trigger for the whole downstream chain.
ComputerEase job status — in-progress, complete, paid — flows back into Salesforce so the operations team stops logging into Cameo and ComputerEase to check milestones (UC7).

stage3.label: Agentic
stage3.headline: AgentForce — Activated
items: "Which Wisconsin jobs posted a deposit below the required 99% threshold this week?" — an AgentForce agent answers it by reading the Salesforce Quote and the contract fields UC3's IDP validation captured, instead of Ashley cross-referencing Home Depot reporting and the signed PDF by hand.

"Which ComputerEase jobs are trending over their budget-worksheet target price before close-out?" — an AgentForce agent reads ComputerEase Job Totals against the budget worksheet UC2 wrote and surfaces margin erosion 30 days early, instead of it being found at close-out. No new vendor and no new procurement cycle — AgentForce runs inside the Salesforce relationship Peerless already owns, reading the exact objects these Year 1 flows create.

journey.closingLine: The Salesforce objects and MuleSoft event triggers established in Year 1 are what AgentForce reads in Year 2. That architecture is decided once.

outcomes.title: Ashley's morning back
outcomes.body: The HD Portal lead check, the 1.5-hour ComputerEase rekey, the document-by-document contract review, and the manual exception comment all stop on go-live day. Her time goes to the work only she can do.

outcomes.title: Legacy ERP, safely connected
outcomes.body: The ComputerEase connection runs through the Deltek-managed CE Live Service relay — identified in week one of scoping — so the integration never touches the GCP VM's external IP. The only firewall change is the MuleSoft tenant allowlist Brian already started.

outcomes.title: AI-Ready Foundation
outcomes.body: Clean, connected, well-maintained data infrastructure is what AI agents need to operate. Every flow we build is a pipeline an AI agent will eventually use — built right from the start.

assumptions.assumption: ComputerEase CE Live Service Relay Installation — Confirm that the Deltek support ticket Jean Jacobs filed on 2026-04-17 is actively in queue. Ensure Deltek support installs the CE Live Service Windows service on the production ComputerEase VM and provides the Deltek-managed integration URL (the API endpoint — NOT the VM external IP). Expect 4-hour minimum SLA per Deltek's legacy-product classification.

ComputerEase Production-Only API Testing Posture — Agree in writing with Peerless leadership AND Deltek that integration testing will occur in PRODUCTION ComputerEase with strictly GET-only access groups until Deltek confirms a dev/sandbox API path. Bundle this confirmation request into the same Deltek support ticket as CE Live Service.

ComputerEase Backup Super-Admin Provisioning (SPOF) — Identify and provision a backup ComputerEase super-admin BEFORE kickoff. Candidate per Ashley Salerno: Laura ('has more access than all of us except for Jean'). Confirm in writing that the backup admin can log in as the PWMAINT system account to create users and grant API access groups. Bundle this with the same Deltek support ticket.

GCP VM Firewall + Static IP Confirmation — (a) Reconcile the canonical static external IP of the ComputerEase production VM — transcripts cite 35.222.218.224 AND 135.226.22218; only one is correct. (b) Lock GCP ingress firewall to the MuleSoft tenant IP allowlist only (pre-engagement state was SSH/RDP open to the entire internet — partially remediated 2026-04-16). (c) Confirm egress firewall permits CE Live Service outbound to the Deltek-managed cloud URL.

HD Portal Write Endpoints + Developer Login — Through Greg (HD account manager), file a single HD ticket bundling: (a) confirm HD Portal exposes POST/PATCH endpoints for comment write-back (UC4) and deposit-paid status (UC5-potential); (b) request a developer-named HD Portal interactive login for DataSkate so the team can inspect HD-side data shape and field-level mappings; (c) confirm document-download endpoints for 299A/299B/HS-118 signed PDFs (UC3). Use Marius as the developer escalation (engaged 15 more days per Ashley 2026-04-16). If HD does not expose write endpoints, plan to fall back to the email channel (Venkat: 'depending upon the endpoint... we can try to mail as well').

about.title: About DataSkate
about.body: DataSkate is an integration partner that builds and operates the MuleSoft data layer underneath a client's existing systems — so the platforms you already own work together without re-platforming any of them. We scope before we sell: in the first week of the Peerless engagement, our architect identified that ComputerEase's API does not live on the GCP VM's external IP and answers only through Deltek's CE Live Service relay on port 445 — the single finding that determines whether this integration works in production. Every flow we build is owned by the client in their own GitHub repository, and every flow is designed as a pipeline an AI agent will eventually read.

snapshot.description: Peerless Fence Group is the largest independently owned fence contractor in the Midwest — a 60+ year, family-founded rollup of regional Illinois/Indiana fencing businesses headquartered in St. Charles, IL, operating across Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, and southern Wisconsin. Acquired January 1, 2023 by Chicago-based private equity firm Akoya Capital Partners as a Home Services platform investment, Peerless has grown through ~10 bolt-on acquisitions since 2013 and now operates its residential pipeline through Home Depot's Pro-contractor channel: leads land in HD Portal, flow into Salesforce CRM, then move to ComputerEase (Deltek) for job costing and accounting.
painPoints: Ashley manually rekeys every closed Salesforce quote into ComputerEase — ~1.5 hours per job (customer number, sequential job number, budget worksheet).
Daily Home Depot reconciliation: Ashley goes through HD reporting by hand to find deposit-paid status and check for new leads.
Document-by-document contract review of HS-105, 299A, 299B, HS-118 against a memorized rule set (price match, legible signatures, Friday dates, Wisconsin 99% deposit).
ComputerEase is a DOS-era legacy ERP (v26.x) with a single super-admin (Jean) and a 4-hour Deltek support SLA — a single point of failure that blocked all access changes for 2 days during PTO.
HD Portal → Salesforce is the missing wire — leads created in Home Depot Service Center don't flow into Salesforce today.

talkingPoints.trigger: When they ask why MuleSoft instead of native Salesforce Flows or a simpler tool
talkingPoints.say: The hard part of this build isn't Salesforce — it's ComputerEase. The API doesn't live on the VM's external IP and it doesn't answer on port 443 or 8081. It runs through a Deltek-managed relay service called CE Live Service that's installed on the same VM, on port 445. Brian found this during our scoping sessions. Every architect who doesn't know that detail will either hit a wall or charge you to discover it. We found it in week one of scoping before we were engaged.
talkingPoints.impact: Prevents 2–4 weeks of dead-end debugging at the ComputerEase integration layer; CE Live Service relay identification is the single biggest risk-reduction milestone in the engagement

Your Tuesday morning changes on day one of production.

talkingPoints.trigger: When Brian asks about the security posture of the integration or about the GCP firewall
talkingPoints.say: The integration doesn't touch your GCP VM's external IP at all. The ComputerEase connection goes to a Deltek-managed URL — that's the CE Live Service relay architecture you identified on April 17th. Once Jean's Deltek support ticket resolves and CE Live Service gets installed, the integration endpoint is Deltek's URL, not your firewall's problem. The MuleSoft tenant IP allowlist on the GCP ingress rule is the only firewall change needed, and you've already started that work.

openingLines.line: Peerless is the Midwest anchor brand for Elevate Fence Partners' six-brand national platform — and the HD Portal to ComputerEase data path that every Home Depot Pro job runs through is the same template your five sibling brands will need when they scale. Brian has been in every scoping session making architecture decisions that are platform-standard, not Peerless-local. So we're scoping the Elevate template today, not just the Peerless instance. Ashley — walk me through what a Tuesday morning looks like, because every manual step you describe is something go-live day removes.

openingLines.context: If they say they already have a plan
openingLines.line: I'll take that and ask one question: does the plan account for the ComputerEase API not living on the GCP VM's external IP? The integration endpoint is a Deltek-managed relay URL routed through CE Live Service — not port 443, not the static IP Brian was debugging. If the plan routes to the VM directly, it'll work in a test environment and fail in production when CE Live Service isn't installed. That's the finding that changes the architecture, and we found it in week one of scoping before code was written.

Every week that doesn't start with UC2 in production is another week Ashley spends 1.5 hours per closed quote manually rekeying Salesforce data into ComputerEase — and the Elevate portfolio integration standard stays unset. Brian Cook has been in every scoping session making platform-architecture decisions. The window where Elevate's Director of IT is actively designing the template that will govern all 6 sibling company codes — and the architecture is still fluid — is the rarest deal-urgency condition we see. The template gets set once. It should be set intentionally.

openingLines.context: AI question — how does this help with AI?
openingLines.line: AgentForce works when there's a clean Salesforce object it can query — a Quote tied to a Lead tied to an HD F-number tied to a ComputerEase job number. Phase 1 builds exactly those joins. Without them, AgentForce can't answer 'which Wisconsin deposits missed 99%' or 'which jobs are trending over budget-worksheet target price before close-out' — Ashley has to open three systems manually to find those answers today. With Phase 1 complete, those questions become AgentForce queries. The Salesforce objects we define in Year 1 are what AgentForce reads. That architecture is decided once.

integrationDeckContent.aiJourneyNarrative: Phase 1 turns HD Portal → Salesforce → ComputerEase into a single instrumented data path: HD Pro leads land in Salesforce within 10 minutes, 'Save as Final' quotes create ComputerEase jobs automatically, and signed HS-105/299A/299B/HS-118 contracts are validated through MuleSoft IDP. Phase 2 makes the Salesforce 'Save as Final' transition the system-of-record trigger for the whole chain — the deposit-paid box Ashley checks by hand in HD reporting syncs back automatically, and ComputerEase job status flows back into Salesforce so the team stops opening Cameo to check milestones. Phase 3 is the agentic endgame for a residential fence contractor: because Year 1 created clean Salesforce objects keyed to HD F-numbers and ComputerEase job numbers, an AgentForce agent can answer 'which Wisconsin deposits missed the 99% threshold this week' or 'which jobs are trending over budget-worksheet target price before close-out' — questions Ashley opens three systems to answer today. The Salesforce objects and MuleSoft triggers defined in Year 1 are exactly what AgentForce reads in Year 2 — that architecture is decided once, and it is the template Brian Cook deploys to all six Elevate company codes.
